settlement.name: Dunadd
settlement.where: centre of the island, the keep on the crag
settlement.flavour: The royal seat. The rock-cut footprint at its gate is where every Dál Riata king has stood.

starts.name: Lissban
starts.where: south of the island, at the road junction below Dunadd
starts.flavour: The lime-washed muster yard below Dunadd's southern gate, where the warbands form before they ever see the sea.

starts.name: Rinnbeg
starts.where: north cape, at the head of the coast road
starts.flavour: A hunters' camp on the north cape, close enough to the cliff edge that the gulls wake you.

starts.name: Tobarglas
starts.where: northeast slope, above the coast road
starts.flavour: A spring-shrine on the eastern slope; the truthspeakers take their first oath over the water.

starts.name: Dromcairn
starts.where: southeast shore — the hamlet beside the island's pier, ~0.5 km southeast of Dunadd
starts.flavour: The cairn on the rise behind the landing, where the bards meet every boat and keep the island's news and its arguments.
starts.corrected: 2026-09-12: the original 'ridge above the ford and windmill' was a misread of the 2k map. The Support Start is a coastal hamlet at the pier; the ford is 0.2 km from Lissban, and the windmill sits 0.35 km east of Dunadd. Name unchanged.

celtic.featureNaming: Gaelic specific + English generic (Daniel 2026-09-13) — 'Owenfinn River', 'Athgorm Ford'. Most are deliberately tautological, the way real Celtic-derived English names are (River Avon = 'river river'). Settlements keep the bare Gaelic; landscape takes the English generic.

features.name: Benlea Mountains
features.where: north-centre of the island, south of Bohermara Road's northern loop
features.flavour: Three summits in a north-east line. The island's roof, and visible from every start.

features.name: Shanderry Forest
features.where: the island's middle, from the mountains' southern foot down to Carrigrua, reaching the west coast at Camasmore Bay
features.flavour: Older than Dunadd, and it knows it.

features.name: Carrigrua
features.where: on Kingshill's eastern shoulder, 0.27 km north-west of Dunadd village
features.flavour: Red roofs on grey stone. Dunadd's fortress — the village grew downhill from its gate.

features.name: The Moyree Lowlands
features.where: east and south-east of Carrigrua, between Shanderry Forest and the eastern shore
features.flavour: The island's only good ploughing, and the only part of it that has ever been quiet.

features.name: Whitemill
features.where: 0.35 km east of Dunadd, standing alone on the Moyree
features.flavour: Lime-washed and visible from the whole vale. The Moyree's clock and its meeting place.

features.name: Kingshill
features.where: immediately west of Carrigrua, Boherath Road crossing its back
features.flavour: The mound the fort stands on. The footprint cut into its crown is where the kings are made — Dunadd is named for this hill, not the other way round.

features.name: Cromcross
features.where: Shanderry Forest's south-east corner, where Bohermara Road turns west for Carrigrua
features.flavour: A waystone at the bend. Every traveller on the island passes it, and most leave something.

features.name: The Bealanard Shoulder
features.where: Benlea's eastern saddle, where Bohermara Road runs closest to the peaks; Tobarglas sits at its foot
features.flavour: The road's high point. From here you see both coasts and the Sidhe island beyond.

features.name: Owenfinn River
features.where: out of Shanderry Forest, south past Carrigrua's western side, then east to the sea near Portcorr
features.flavour: Fast, shallow and clear. It cuts the island in two, and the halves do not much like each other.

features.name: Athgorm Ford
features.where: on Boherath Road, 0.22 km north-east of Lissban
features.flavour: Cold, shallow, and the only dry way south. It floods twice a winter.

features.name: Portcorr
features.where: the south-east shore at the Owenfinn's mouth, 0.31 km east of Dromcairn
features.flavour: The island's only pier. Every boat off Dál Riata leaves from it, including the one to Tara.

features.name: Camasmore Bay
features.where: the west coast at mid-island, where Shanderry Forest comes down to the water
features.flavour: Wide, scalloped and sheltered. The cliffs at its southern end hold Uaimh na Scáth.

features.name: Cuaseen
features.where: the island's north tip, beside Rinnbeg
features.flavour: Room for four boats and no more. The first water a northern Celt ever rows.

features.name: Kyleshee Strait
features.where: the water between Dál Riata and the Sidhe island to the west
features.flavour: Tara is visible across it on a clear day. Nobody crosses it casually.

features.name: Muirmore Sea
features.where: the open water east of Dál Riata, toward the Germanic coast
features.flavour: Realm-level water — it touches Germanic, Alfar, Romance and Baltic shores too.
features.status: provisional — belongs to the realm pass; other cultures should have their own word for it

features.name: Blunt Head
features.where: the south-west peninsula; Lissban sits on its neck
features.flavour: Low, bare and square to the weather. The first land a boat from the south sees.

features.name: Grey Head
features.where: the north-east corner, where Bohermara Road turns south
features.flavour: Grey rock through green turf. Answers Blunt Head at the island's other corner.

features.name: Bohermara Road
features.where: from Rinnbeg at the north tip, down the whole east shore, to Cromcross
features.flavour: Never out of sight of water. Links Rinnbeg, Tobarglas and the Bealanard Shoulder.

features.name: Boherath Road
features.where: from Carrigrua south over Athgorm Ford to Lissban, then east to Portcorr
features.flavour: The island's southern half in one line.

features.name: Garveen Shallows
features.where: the sandbars and breakers ringing the island's coasts
features.flavour: Good fishing, bad sailing. Wrecks on the western side going back further than Dunadd.

dungeons.name: Uaimh na Scáth
dungeons.sense: uaimh + na + scáth — 'the cave of the shadows'
dungeons.grammarNote: Irish never eclipses s (the pairs are b→mb, c→gc, d→nd, f→bhf, g→ng, p→bp, t→dt), so the earlier 'na dScáth' is not valid. 'na Scáth' reads as an archaic genitive plural; strict modern Irish would be 'na Scáthanna'.
dungeons.nameUsage: Irish is the formal/map name; 'Cave of Shadows' is the common name players use. It is the one name on Dál Riata an English speaker will not get right on sight — deliberate, for the dungeon only.
dungeons.where: the sea cliffs at the southern end of Camasmore Bay, on the west coast below Shanderry Forest — the far side of the island from Portcorr and the starts

acts.name: the outer caves
acts.inhabitants: Fomorian raiders — sea-giants beached in the tidal caves
acts.note: their coastal camp outside the mouth is the level 8-10 outdoor approach (Phase 4's Fomorian raider family), teaching the mechanics the dungeon tests

acts.name: the dark behind
acts.note: what the Fomorians are squatting beside, and why they are jumpy. Ties to the Sidhe across Kyleshee Strait and to Phase 4's fae creature in the northern wood.

dungeons.flavour: The tide goes into the cliff further than it comes out. The raiders took the front of it and will not sleep past the second turn.

settlement.name: Tara
settlement.where: west of the island, below the mountain
settlement.flavour: The many-spired seat of the Sidhe.

starts.name: Ardshee
starts.where: northeast ridge, above the eastern coast
starts.flavour: A fairy-mound on the eastern ridge; the whispers go out from it with the wind at their back.

starts.name: Aislin
starts.where: mid-island, east of the mountain spine
starts.flavour: A still hollow where the muses and philosophers are taught to trust what they see asleep.

starts.name: Carrowdoon
starts.where: south of the island, by the cave mouth above the strand
starts.flavour: The cave-hall on the southern strand; shield-line and healers share one fire and one watch.

settlement.name: Miklagarðr
settlement.where: north head of the range, in the frost forest
settlement.flavour: The great copper-roofed city at the head of the mountains.

secondarySettlements.name: Hedeby
secondarySettlements.where: east of the range, on the trading water below the passes

starts.name: Jarnborg
starts.where: centre of the range, at the black forge-keep in the pass
starts.flavour: The black forge-keep holding the central pass; the shieldmen are made here, in both senses.

starts.name: Grimstrand
starts.where: east coast, at the great gabled hall north of Hedeby
starts.flavour: The long hall on the eastern strand where the hunters land and the seeresses read the tide.

starts.name: Skaldfell
starts.where: south of Hedeby, high in the white peaks
starts.flavour: A windmill hamlet in the peaks; every Germanic song worth singing was first sung badly here.

settlement.name: Vetrholt
settlement.where: centre of the Alfar lowland, under the treeline
settlement.flavour: The Alfar hall-town, roofed in split shingle that never quite loses its rime.

starts.name: Frostvik
starts.where: northwest coast, at the lakeside village
starts.flavour: The white-shingle inlet; muses and hunters share the same pier and the same bad weather.

starts.name: Steinvard
starts.where: southwest, at the bridge and windmill on the south coast
starts.flavour: The bridge-fort at the southern crossing, the one place the Alfar have never yielded.

starts.name: Brunnstead
starts.where: southeast, at the coastal village and dock
starts.flavour: The dock beside the meltwater spring the Alfar healers draw from and carry out.

hillback-dwarves.tongue: invented — brak stone, gorn iron, mor hold/seat, ruk works/camp

settlement.name: Brakmor
settlement.where: northeast, the great round tower crowning the pass
settlement.flavour: The Hillback Empire is run out of one room in it.

starts.name: Gornruk
starts.where: the terraced camp at Brakmor's foot
starts.flavour: No Hillback begins inside the hold; you earn the door.

settlement.name: Laukapils
settlement.where: east, the stone keep and its orange-roofed town
settlement.flavour: Ringed by windmills on the dry plain.

starts.name: Ozolkalns
starts.where: north, at the lone great tree on the rise
starts.flavour: One enormous oak; Baltic shieldmen are sworn under it and nowhere else.

starts.name: Saltinis
starts.where: northwest coast, the small orange-roofed hamlet
starts.flavour: The wise-women boil their herbs within sight of the water.

starts.name: Vilkupe
starts.where: west coast, the camp at the river mouth
starts.flavour: The scouts and the agitators both claim they named it.

settlement.name: Borograd
settlement.where: east, the farm town with the white church
settlement.flavour: The largest settled place on the eastern plain.

starts.name: Vukoves
starts.where: northwest, the kiln camp in the foothills under the white peaks
starts.flavour: Charcoal-burners' kilns; you learn to move quietly because of the smoke, not the wolves.

starts.name: Studenbrod
starts.where: west, the camp at the stream crossing
starts.flavour: Holds the western crossing and the road tax nobody admits to paying.

starts.name: Kamenles
starts.where: south, the palisaded longhouse and tents at the forest edge
starts.flavour: The shield-line and its preachers muster together.

slavic.note: Daniel 2026-09-12: confirmed all four archetypes are covered here. The 'Damage Support' marker at Vukoves carries Damage; the dedicated 'Support Start' at Studenbrod carries Support, which is how byArchetype resolves them.

settlement.name: Crucivallum
settlement.where: centre of the map, the five-sided moat-wall and grey citadel
settlement.flavour: The polity label 'Crusader Empire' stays; this is what the city itself is called.

starts.name: Tirocastra
starts.where: inside the western wall, the tent lines and round drill-ring
starts.flavour: Everyone the Empire will ever use passes through it.

settlement.name: Valmonde
settlement.where: south, the hill town in the orchard country
settlement.flavour: Italics Romana is the region; Valmonde is who runs it.

starts.name: Marvigne
starts.where: north coast, the terraced red-roofed hamlet
starts.flavour: The syndicates weigh every cargo twice.

starts.name: Pierregarde
starts.where: west, the black stone fort below the mountains
starts.flavour: It takes the road-toll and the first fight, in that order.

starts.name: Fontcalme
starts.where: centre, the walled manor on the hill road
starts.flavour: Squires and preachers learn their letters and their bandages in the same hour.

mythic.tongue: Greek, archaic — APPROVED by Daniel 2026-09-12. Rationale: Equal and Pankrator are rollable only by Hellenic, Mythic and one outlier each; among the eight human cultures only Hellenic rolls either, and among the three elf races only Mythic does. Completes the elf-pairs-with-human pattern (Sidhe/Celtic/Irish, Alfar/Germanic/Norse). The map places Mythic Territory in the western vastwood rather than beside Hellenic, so they read as the older withdrawn branch.

settlement.name: Argyrion
settlement.where: deep in the western vastwood, the lone white spire
settlement.flavour: Visible from nowhere except directly below.

starts.name: Anthemon
starts.where: south edge of the wood, the tent camp on the golden hills
starts.flavour: Where the Mythic send their young out into the light for the first time.

settlement.name: Leukopolis
settlement.where: east, the marble terraces and round theatre above the lake
settlement.flavour: Marble terraces stepping down to the water.

starts.name: Aspidon
starts.where: northwest, the river village at the mountain gate
starts.flavour: The line forms in its square every dawn whether or not anything is coming.

starts.name: Palaistron
starts.where: northeast, the villas above the aqueduct
starts.flavour: Pankrators are broken in and equals are made.

starts.name: Mouseion
starts.where: south bank of the river
starts.flavour: Argument is the local industry.

starts.name: Panakeia
starts.where: east, the temple complex above the lake
starts.flavour: The only building in the territory nobody has ever fought over.

settlement.name: Lusavank
settlement.where: centre, the conical-domed church and village above the lake

starts.name: Berdkar
starts.where: west, the camp on the water at the Bloom's edge
starts.flavour: The Bloom stops here, because the Armenians stop it.

starts.name: Arevtun
starts.where: northeast, the farmstead and chapel on the terrace above Lusavank
starts.flavour: The sunny terrace; everything grown here is grown twice a year.

starts.name: Surbhogi
starts.where: south, the shrine-camp on the lakeshore inside the Bloom
starts.flavour: The preachers tend the ones the Bloom has already touched.

woodling.tongue: invented — -knot a settled thicket, -burr a sheltered hollow, -mott a scout copse

starts.name: Mossburr
starts.where: west, the lakeside hollow behind the fence line
starts.flavour: Everything green in Woodling medicine grows within fifty paces of it.

starts.name: Thornmott
starts.where: east, in the open boulder country
starts.flavour: A scout copse, deliberately uncomfortable.

woodling.note: No Frontline start because Woodling has no Frontline class. Not a gap.

gobbledrift.tongue: invented — -drift a wandering camp, -glim a hearth-place

settlement.name: Rattledrift
settlement.flavour: The biggest and loudest of the Gobbledrift camps, which is how it became the capital. It has moved four times.

starts.name: Tinglim
starts.where: east, the boulder overhang in the dry scrub
starts.flavour: A hearth roofed in salvaged sheet. Warm, bright, and audible from a long way off.

gobbledrift.note: Gobbledrift can only roll Support and DPS classes; the two nulls are correct.

fae.tongue: invented — -bell a seat or hall, -wisp a camp, -glass a still pool

settlement.name: Hollowbell
settlement.where: centre of the Bloom, southeast of the map
settlement.flavour: Named for the note the crystal flowers make before a storm.

starts.name: Quickenwisp
starts.where: centre-south of the Bloom
starts.flavour: A rowan camp — quicken-wood, the old ward against fae mischief, which the Fae find funny. The volvas keep the ward and the shield-line keeps the volvas.

starts.name: Dewglass
starts.where: east of the Bloom
starts.flavour: A still pool that holds the reflection a second longer than it should. Whatever the Fae send out hunting goes out from here, and checks itself in the water first.

fae.note: Daniel 2026-09-12: Fae has exactly two markers and they double up — Healer rides with Frontline at Quickenwisp, Damage rides with Support at Dewglass. All four archetypes covered.

centaur.tongue: invented — -mane a seat, -run a road or course

settlement.name: Longmane
settlement.where: northeast shoulder of the plateau, the red-roofed hall
settlement.flavour: The Centaur seat above the elder wood.

starts.name: Archrun
starts.where: the plateau's north edge, beneath the old aqueduct arches
starts.flavour: Every Centaur's first gallop is the length of it, and they all remember the time.

centaur.note: Centaur has no Support class (Knight, Squire, Preacher, Equal, Frontiersman, Whisper); the null is correct.

regions.name: Crusader Empire
regions.note: the pentagon polity; its city is Crucivallum

regions.name: Italics Romana
regions.note: Romance heartland region; its seat is Valmonde

regions.name: Thracian Frontier
regions.note: mountain march between the Empire and the Hellenic lands; no start points

regions.name: Castrated Plains
regions.note: blighted plain east of the Empire; no start points

regions.name: Dew Hollow
regions.note: culture-group region spanning Woodling, Gobbledrift, Fae and Centaur territories

settled: Dunadd stands as the Dál Riata seat; Dunlaith rejected.
Mythic keeps the Greek register (Argyrion, Anthemon).
Miklagarðr is the Germanic capital for spawn/hearth purposes; Hedeby is the second town.
Slavic and Baltic each cover all four archetypes.
Fae's two markers each carry two archetypes.
Woodling has no Frontline class and Centaur no Support class; those nulls are correct.
openQuestions: Lore hook, unclaimed: who built the aqueduct through Centaur country, and why does it run toward Dew Hollow?
